recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Further edits for FHIR-11089 would either reverse later Patient Care decisions or add redundant editorial wording; any future assertedDate work should be handled in the Extension Pack or by a new Patient Care decision.
issue_request: FHIR-11089 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care request to address DSTU2-era naming inconsistencies between AllergyIntolerance and Condition: keep AllergyIntolerance.patient and Condition.subject, resolve status naming through the same block vote, change AllergyIntolerance.reporter to asserter with RelatedPerson support, rename AllergyIntolerance.attestedDate and Condition.dateRecorded to assertedDate, and make AllergyIntolerance.onset polymorphic.
initial_application: The issue was directly applied by git commit ed170ff0754268f2a677a011f9d432d1328415f0, whose message cites #11089 and synchronized Condition and AllergyIntolerance elements for asserter, assertedDate, and onset while also applying the related AllergyIntolerance status split from FHIR-11151.
additional_context: AllergyIntolerance and Condition are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Later FHIR-17285 moved assertedDate from the core resources to extensions and added recordedDate to both resources; those assertedDate extensions are now in the FHIR Extension Pack. FHIR-34395 temporarily replaced recorder/asserter with participant, but later FHIR-39513, FHIR-39602, and FHIR-44517 restored explicit recorder/asserter elements for the current R6 source.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current core source has AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus and verificationStatus, AllergyIntolerance.patient, Condition.subject with Patient or Group targets, AllergyIntolerance.onset[x], recordedDate on both resources, and explicit recorder/asserter elements with RelatedPerson support. A git grep found no active legacy attestedDate, dateRecorded, or AllergyIntolerance.reporter XML elements under the AllergyIntolerance or Condition source directories.
